hints: Focus on the phrase small circular DNA. This is not the long linear DNA in the nucleus, so ask yourself which organelles carry their own tiny circular genomes.

P has only one sequence type but Q has two different sequence types. Think about which plant cell has only mitochondria, and which green photosynthetic cell has mitochondria plus a second DNA-containing organelle.
walkthrough:
**Spot What Small Circular DNA Means**

In eukaryotic cells, small circular DNA is found outside the nucleus. It is the genome of mitochondria, and in plants, also of chloroplasts.

So the question is really asking: does the cell have one type of DNA-containing organelle or two types?

**Decode P Versus Q**

Cell P has circular DNA all with the same sequence. That suggests only one population of organelles, so only mitochondria.

Cell Q has two different sequences of circular DNA. That suggests two different populations of organelles, so mitochondria plus chloroplasts.

**Match To Root and Leaf**

A non-photosynthetic plant cell, like a root cortical cell, has mitochondria but no chloroplasts. That fits P perfectly.

A photosynthetic plant cell, like a leaf mesophyll cell, has both mitochondria and chloroplasts. That fits Q perfectly with its two types of circular DNA.

options.A: Both heart muscle fibres and root cortical cells have mitochondria but no chloroplasts, so both would show only one type of circular DNA, not two types in Q.
options.B: Lymphocytes have mitochondrial DNA, but mature red blood cells have no mitochondria and no circular DNA of their own, so P and Q do not fit.
options.C: Mature red blood cells have lost their nucleus and mitochondria, so they contain no small circular DNA, and sieve tube elements also lack the mitochondria plus chloroplast combination.
options.D: Root cortical cells have only mitochondrial circular DNA (one sequence type for P), while leaf mesophyll cells have both mitochondrial and chloroplast circular DNA (two sequence types for Q).
